newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters welcomes hearing over Banks dispute.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters welcomes hearing over Banks dispute.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters on Wednesday welcomed parliamentary speaker Doug Kidd's decision to refer his dispute with National Party backbench MP John Banks to parliament's privileges committee.

"I am happy with the Speaker's decision. There have been a lot of wild and woolly statements being made about this matter and I look forward to the privileges committee hearing, where I will defend myself vigorously," Peters told Reuters.
He said the matter was now sub-judice and he would not comment on details of the allegations.

The Speaker found that a question of privilege was involved and the committee should consider an allegation made by Alliance leader Jim Anderton that Peters assaulted Banks in a corridor of parliament after the House adjourned on March 5.
Peters denies assaulting Banks but last week tendered an unreserved apology for upsetting him.
The privileges committee will determine the facts and any culpability over the incident.
Parliament appointed the membership of the privileges committee in February but it is yet to meet and elect a chairperson.
Its members are Prime Minister Jim Bolger, Peters, Anderton, Attorney-General Paul East, Justice Minister Doug Graham, and Labour MPs Michael Cullen, Lianne Dalziel and Jonathan Hunt.
It is likely East will be elected to chair the committee.
Clerk-assistant of parliament's select committees Mary Harris said the speaker would set the time for the committee's first meeting.
Evidence presented at committees is normally given in public, but can be given in privacy or secrecy if the committee unanimously agrees.
